sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file header rules
sections.what: Brings in the project and evidence types, the shared field list, the locator helper, and the duration calculation. The header states that the file is read-only and never guesses values.
sections.why: Likely reason: the header states the rules so future edits keep them.
sections.watch_out: The duration calculation is imported from outside the api-server folder, so moving that library breaks this file.

sections.name: ScanEvidenceField
sections.title: Shape of one evidence-backed value
sections.what: Defines a field that carries its value along with where it came from: web address, publisher, the quote, and a locator.
sections.why: Likely reason: every scan field uses this same shape, so the scan can show sources the same way.
sections.watch_out: Every part can be null, so readers must check each part before showing it.

sections.name: ScanCapacity
sections.title: Shape of capacity
sections.what: Defines capacity as a number with an optional unit.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A unit can be missing while a value exists, so unit text is not guaranteed.

sections.name: ProjectScanData, FIELD_BY_KEY
sections.title: Full shape of one project record
sections.what: Describes every part of one project's scan record, including cost, schedule, capacity, and location-style fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed layout lets the scan rely on the same structure for every project.
sections.watch_out: The forecast flag, technology, and companies entries are optional, so older saved runs may not include them.

sections.name: evidenceField
sections.title: Builds one evidence-backed field
sections.what: Turns a field's value and its matching evidence into one shape. If there is no value and no evidence, the field becomes null.
sections.why: Likely reason: a value with no evidence still appears, but without a source.
sections.watch_out: Zero counts as a real value, and only null, undefined, or empty text count as missing.

sections.name: field
sections.title: Looks up a field and its evidence
sections.what: Finds the field description by key, picks the matching evidence, and builds the evidence-backed field.
sections.why: Likely reason: every field uses this one lookup, so the logic lives in one place.
sections.watch_out: The lookup asserts that the key exists, so a mistyped key fails with an error when the record is built.

sections.name: buildProjectScanData
sections.title: Assembles one project's scan record
sections.what: Builds the full record for one project: capacity, company list, cost, schedule, and location-style fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: one function keeps the record layout in one place.
sections.watch_out: The duration basis text states that months are days divided by a fixed number, so that text must change if the calculation changes.

sections.name: buildScanData
sections.title: Builds records for many projects
sections.what: Runs the single-project builder for each project, using an empty evidence list when a project has none.
sections.why: Likely reason: one call gives the scan every project's record.
sections.watch_out: Projects without evidence still appear, with their values but without sources.

summary: Builds a read-only record for each project for the Benchmark Scan feature, where any value or evidence the app does not have is shown as null rather than guessed.
purpose: Turns each project row and its evidence rows into one stable shape that the scan can read, without changing the database.
why: Likely reason: a stable shape lets the scan rely on the same fields for every project. The file header states that it never fabricates values.
how: First it reads the project's capacity. Then it fills each cost, schedule, and location-style field by pairing the project value with the matching evidence. Missing values and missing evidence both become null. Finally it returns one record per project, and the list version runs this for every project it receives.
inputs: A list of project records from the database, and a map from each project id to its evidence quotes.
outputs: A list of per-project records holding id, name, industry, cost, schedule, capacity, and location-style fields. Each field carries a value and its source details.
risks: Stored values pass through unchanged, so a wrong number reaches the scan without any warning. The file trusts that the evidence map is keyed by project id.
debug: If a field is null when it should have a value, check its entry in the field list file and its evidence labels. If the planned duration is missing, check the stored duration and the construction and completion dates. If a whole project is missing, check that its id appears in the evidence map.
